original.target_description: Original Experiment 2, number of women named summed over four questions; masculine generics versus both alternative generic conditions pooled.

n.sample_role: Participants in the primary Experiment 2 contrast spanning all three randomized language conditions; 45 female and 45 male participants.
n.exclusions: Primary analysis includes all 90 described participants. Note 3 reports a separate sensitivity rerun excluding four capital-I respondents; its revised statistics are not supplied.

notes: Identity checked independently from article title NAME YOUR FAVORITE MUSICIAN / Effects of Masculine Generics and of Their Alternatives in German, authors Dagmar Stahlberg, Sabine Sczesny, Friederike Braun, journal Vol. 20 No. 4 December 2001 pp. 464-469. These match the original reference. The DOI is not printed in the supplied text and was not independently resolved. Supplied candidate is an author-provided ResearchGate full-text HTML extraction, containing the article through notes and references, not merely an abstract; no PDF is supplied. Trailing book-review text is unrelated and excluded. All extraction concerns original Experiment 2; replication/pilot/extension qualifiers in some neutral descriptions do not change the assigned original-side primary study. Unassigned fields and replication/reported_success are placeholders. Identified test: masculine generics versus both alternative generic conditions pooled. Same-test printed p retained as candidate evidence only because p is unassigned here: p < .01. Three condition means are printed (2.37, 2.67, 4.60, respectively); no raw mean difference or standardized effect or test statistic is printed for this contrast. The omnibus F(2,84)=9.97 is a distinct test and is not substituted. Analytic N derivation for the all-condition primary contrast: 45 female + 45 male = 90 participants. Sex groups are mutually exclusive; all three randomized language conditions enter this contrast. Four respondents were removed only for the separate sensitivity rerun; no sensitivity result is extracted.
